speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head M of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Mr Chairman, in his Budget speech, Prime Minister Wong highlighted that we are entering a post-SG60 chapter of Singapore's development in a world that is becoming more uncertain and more contested.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In such an environment, stewardship of our fiscal resources becomes even more critical.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Singapore's fiscal credibility remains one of our strongest foundations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Maintaining prudent budgetary policies and effective governance ensures that we preserve a strong financial base not only for ourselves, but for future generations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is especially important, giving rising structural spending pressures from ageing, healthcare, climate resilience and security.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Globally, many governments are also facing increasingly constrained fiscal positions as these pressures build.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, but stewardship is not only about restraint.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is also about ensuring that every dollar is used effectively.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Prudent governance must therefore be continuous, not episodic.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In this regard, I would like to see clarification from the Minister.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How is MOF strengthening scrutiny over high-value projects and deepening programme evaluation frameworks to ensure major initiatives deliver measurable outcomes over time?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Beyond the initial approval, are there structured review mechanisms to allow resources to be re-allocated dynamically, particularly where programmes no longer meet intended objectives or where priorities have shifted?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It would be useful if the Ministry could share concrete examples of such re-allocations in recent years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, finance should also be a catalyst for innovation and transformation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I therefore welcome efforts to support community partnerships and new delivery models, including through the Singapore Government Partnerships Office.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In areas such as ageing, mental health and family resilience, early and preventive interventions can reduce significantly higher downstream costs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Could the Minister share how MOF evaluates the long-term fiscal impact of such investments?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are there frameworks that go beyond immediate expenditure to capture medium- and long-term cost avoidance as well as broader social returns?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, as part of responsible fiscal stewardship, we must also periodically review structural features of our tax system.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Our system has served us well and we should preserve its fundamental strengths.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At the same time, structural parameters should evolve alongside economic realities.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: During the recent People's Action Party (PAP) Policy Forum discussions, participants suggested reviewing the income tax relief structures against updated median incomes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: More than two decades on, the context has changed materially.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As incomes rise while thresholds remain static, bracket creep occurs gradually.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: More lower- and middle-income earners enter the tax space, not necessarily because they are significantly better off, but because the system has not been recalibrated.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Otherwise, bracket creep becomes a silent shift in the tax burden – one that is not always visible but is nonetheless felt.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The point is not to call for tax cuts.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A periodic review of such structural thresholds can help ensure that the original policy intent of protecting lower- and middle-income earners remains intact.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Any adjustments, if considered, can be calibrated and phased and implemented in a fiscally responsible manner.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In this way, we preserve both fairness and sustainability.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I would therefore encourage the Ministry to, beyond this, periodically assess whether such structural parameters remain appropriately aligned with today's income distribution and tax structure going forward.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, strong fiscal stewardship requires three things – discipline in how we spend, rigour in how we evaluate, and adaptability in how we design our systems.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If we continue to strengthen this, we will not only preserve our fiscal position, but also reinforce trust in our system across generations.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, as a capital exporter, Singapore should manage our national capital to build a network economy, shifting from a gross domestic product (GDP) to a gross national product (GNP) mindset.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What can our capital, enterprises and people produce for Singapore across the world?

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The recent restructuring of Temasek Holdings provides a timely opportunity to manage this capital more effectively and strategically.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Pathway one – strategy investing in global norms.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Let us invest in sectors where Singapore lacks the natural advantages.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Emerging domains like space technology are prime examples.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: By positioning ourselves as a critical node in these high-value ecosystems through targeted research and development, and global partnerships, we secure our position and our relevance in the future economy.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must leverage the new Temasek-Singapore restructuring as a portfolio to create a Singapore pack.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our national champions should act as anchors, pulling our smaller enterprises into global supply chains and opening doors that our small and medium enterprises (SMEs) cannot knock on alone.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As we invest globally, can we build structured overseas pathways for Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Not student exchanges, not internships, but good jobs from early career to mid-career, leveraging the host country networks that our sovereign investments can help create.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Placing Singaporeans overseas seeds the nodes of our global network, returning with relationships and experiences to drive our network economy.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In closing, Mr Chairman, as a small city-state, we must capture value across global networks.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: By managing our capital exports strategically, we strengthen our future economy, we grow our enterprise ecosystem and generate good jobs for Singaporeans at home and abroad.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong, you may take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: A constituent I visited is a retiree in his home for decades – asset rich, cash poor.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: His landed home is one of the most basic in the area.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: His neighbour tells a different story – rebuilt into a multi-storey house; three units, three entrances, three tenants and a very high rental yield.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: His neighbourhood gentrified around him while he stayed put.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: A retiree who never rented and never will is taxed as a landlord.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: In February 2024, the same concern was raised – how the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) assesses AV for asset-rich but cash-poor owners.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The response was that IRAS considers "improvement works last done." But his problem is not his property's condition.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Capital value – based on sales, not rentals.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: It would better reflect the position of owner-occupiers who derive no rental income.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The Government rejected this, citing fewer sales transactions and greater price volatility.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Why does this reasoning not apply to the Chief Valuer's other function?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: When the Chief Valuer prices state land for Build-To-Order flats, the methodology references resale flat transactions – this was confirmed by the Government in November 2025.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Will the Government consider capital value for owner-occupied property tax?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Last year, my colleague, Louis Chua, asked whether the administrative concession allowing hotels and restaurants to display prices excluding GST and service charge was still relevant.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The Minister replied that he did not think consumers would be confused.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: But in 2022, IRAS had to clamp down on restaurants that were imposing nominal service charges – as low as 0.1% – specifically to exploit this loophole and avoid displaying GST inclusive prices.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: These establishments were gaming the system to advertise lower prices while adding the charges at the end.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: If consumers were truly not confused by this practice, why did IRAS need to take enforcement action?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The real problem is that this exemption creates a perverse incentive.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: It is a competitive advantage that comes at the expense of price transparency.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: IRAS justifies this concession by saying it helps restaurants manage pricing differences between dine-in and takeaway orders.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: It is just as easy to display a full price and subtract a 10% discount for takeaway as it is to display a lower price and add a 10% service charge for dine-in.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The arithmetic is identical, only the direction changes.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: In an age of electronic menus and ordering systems, it is anachronistic to cite the cost of printing paper menus as justification for denying consumers basic price transparency.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: I urge IRAS to conduct a proper public feedback exercise.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: First, assess consumer demand for clear display of GST-inclusive prices.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Second, estimate the actual cost to hotels and restaurants of modifying their menus and ordering systems.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Let the evidence, not assumptions made three decades ago, determine whether this concession still serves any public interest or whether it simply allows businesses to advertise artificially low prices at the expense of consumer clarity.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: (In Mandarin): Over the past few months, SME owners have told me that it is not that there are no orders, but the customers are placing orders more cautiously with shorter cycles.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: They also say that what worries them most is not the hard work, but the uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Therefore, prudent fiscal policy is not just a macroeconomic principle but also foundation for providing stable expectations for businesses.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Over the years, the Government has accumulated national reserves and made good use of the Net Investment Return Contribution (NIRC) to support national development and helping families and businesses to weather difficult times.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I believe the key is not just the numbers, but how we utilise this space to strengthen the business confidence to support SME upgrading and transformation whilst reserving buffers for potential future risks.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Minister to clarify two points.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Second, within the framework of emphasising intergenerational equity, how do we ensure that today's fiscal decisions not only avoid burdening the next generation but also preserve sufficient policy flexibility and response capacity for future businesses?

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Mr Chairman, prudent fiscal policy is not just about safeguarding the books but about safeguarding business confidence and also employment stability as well as Singapore's long-term economic resilience.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The Chairman: Ms Tin Pei Ling, you may take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: They protect consumers, deter unfair and illicit practices and support healthy industry development.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: In Singapore, our strong regulatory framework upholds integrity, safety and fair markets, yet compliance also imposes direct expenses, administrative burdens and slower decision cycles.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: For instance, complex or changing regulations often force companies to recruit additional compliance specialists, roles that can be hard to fill, raising recruitment and headcount costs while still leaving compliance challenges unresolved.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: These reduce operational flexibility and lengthen wait times.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Smaller firms and fast‑moving businesses are hit the hardest.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Businesses face real hurdles in cross‑border trade – divergent rules and standards across countries, cumbersome paperwork, limited access to trade finance, fragmented and inefficient payment systems and incompatible data standards and systems.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: These frictions are amplified by a volatile geopolitical environment – unilateral measures, such as the sudden US tariff changes are a stark example.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Firms need swift movement of goods and settlement of payments.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: They cannot afford to be hit by unexpected sudden policy changes or tariff shocks while their cargo or cash is in transit.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: With a limited domestic market, they must internationalise.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Cross‑border frictions, however, add to their cost pressures and constrain their ability to scale.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Single Window was thus welcomed.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Ng Shi Xuan, you may take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Today, the Personal Income Tax is the third largest source of Government revenue.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Through our PAP Policy Forum engagement as Mr Saktiandi, and from what I see in Naval Base constituency, many dual-income middle-class families feel stretched.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: They pay tax, may not qualify for direct transfers, yet support children, ageing parents and fulfil national duty.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: They ask me, can we do something about it?

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: So, I would like to suggest tax credits for two groups of Singaporeans: National Servicemen (NSmen) and caregivers.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Under our current release and using a median dual-income household earning about $12,000 per month as an example, one spouse earning $72,000 may claim about $24,000 to $31,000 in parent, child and NSman reliefs, depending on how many dependents one may have.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Tax falls from about $2,800 to about $550.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: A $1,000 deduction saves $115 at 11.5%, but only $70 at 7%.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: And these would provide meaningful and equal recognition regardless of our tax bracket.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: With SAF60 approaching in 2027, this could be an appropriate juncture to recognise our NSmen and with the Budget surplus, it is a timely window to pilot such calibrated credits.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: With the recent Budget surplus, we have an opportunity to make careful reinvestments that raise productivity across our economy.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Some businesses have shared that they are adjusting to cost pressures from increases in Local Qualifying Salary and foreign worker levies.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: These are important structural moves to uplift wages and productivity.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: But we must also help businesses bring in more revenue and compete more effectively.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: One practical way to do so is through how to leverage AI in Government procurement.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: But this is not to say that all the work must be done by the Government.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: We will be giving AI subscription support for individuals in this Budget.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: In this same spirit, could we also pilot —

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Mr Chairman, I will try to do better with time.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: I declare my interest as Group Managing Director of Commonwealth Capital Group.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: While the vast majority of our conglomerate’s revenues are with retail customers and private businesses, there may be occasions where some of our investee companies serve the Government as a customer.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: It also disburses significant sums in the form of grants, much of it goes to SMEs.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Given its heft, the Government can shape the rules of the game to support our local enterprises: one, by taking a leadership role in adopting new technologies to improve efficiency; two, by shaping market norms and business practices, and three, by reducing unnecessary frictions when interacting with the Government.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: To this end, the Ministry could consider the following.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: First, rethink how the Government interacts with businesses.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Let us not ask companies to navigate the Government but instead ask how the Government can proactively use technologies to guide companies in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: At the front-end, GoBusiness and the Business Grants Portal are good first steps.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: But they still require companies to sift through a smorgasbord of policies and pick out the relevant ones.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Instead of relying only on SME Centres, can we go further with AI?

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Based on their parameters, such as scale, industry and markets, companies could receive bespoke recommendations on applying for upcoming tenders or relevant grants; get customised real-time updates on how policy changes impact their business; and ask questions about how investment or hiring decisions would impact their payouts from the Government under all relevant policies.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Second, on the back-end, it currently takes between four to 10 weeks to process grant applications.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Could our public servants use AI tools to expedite these assessments?

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Third, adopt more pro-business payment terms and disbursement schedules, which should be at negligible cost to the Government.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Some grants, like the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, can be paid earlier and more frequently, instead of only once a year.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: This would have an immaterial impact on the Government’s cashflow but could make a difference to our cash-strapped local companies.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Mr Chairman, the Government operates at a scale which no local enterprise can match.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: It is best placed to invest in the right technology and processes to support our local enterprises to succeed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Chairman, let me speak on two areas where MOF can lead meaningful transformation: inclusive procurement and AI-enabled fiscal governance.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On inclusive procurement, beyond its current emphases on transparency and quality, MOF can better support SMEs with three refinements.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This addresses cash-flow pressures preventing capable SMEs from bidding.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Second, smarter contract packaging by avoiding monolithic tenders where feasible.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Disaggregating components like cybersecurity or design allows SMEs to compete in their strengths whilst maintaining programme coordination.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Third, recognising social value in contracts through a points system similar to weightage in sustainability contracts.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Modest weight could reward verifiable contributions like skills transfer, disability employment or SME participation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Hence, differentiating proposals that strengthen our societal ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On AI-enabled fiscal governance, MOF can harness AI to meet rising transaction volumes and accountability expectations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: First, better forecasting using machine learning to analyse economic indicators, demographics and trade trends for more accurate budget forecasts.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Second, improved compliance through AI-powered smart forms and real-time compliance checkers, strengthening governance whilst reducing administrative workloads.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Third, sharper resource allocation by analysing which programmes deliver greatest public value per dollar.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: By refining procurement and harnessing AI, we can strengthen enterprises, embed social value recognition and ensure fiscal system robustness.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling, you may take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Lower friction encourages broader participation and stronger competition.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Second, can the Ministry trial AI tools to strengthen procurement finance, audit and administration?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: AI can flag anomalies, speed up verification and reduce manual processing, while maintaining strong governance.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: By modernising GeBIZ, we can make Government procurement faster, smarter and more aligned with our economic and social priorities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Government procurement must not only deliver value for money, it must also create fair opportunities for our SMEs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Many smaller tech firms have strong capabilities in digital solutions, cybersecurity and AI, but struggle to compete in large, bundled ICT tenders due to scale and track record requirements.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: At the same time, clearer project scoping and sensible risk allocation will help SMEs participate with confidence, without overextending themselves.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: By widening access to ICT procurement opportunities, we support enterprise growth, deepen competition and build greater resilience into our public sector's digital transformations.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairman, I rise to speak on two areas under MOF's purview.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While each operate within its own governance structure, differences in scale and investment capabilities may lead to uneven outcomes over time.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Second, I wish to address grant disbursement timelines that directly impacts businesses' cash flow.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Progressive Wage Credit Scheme is an important measure supporting lower wage workers.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, annual disbursements may create interim cash flow pressures for SMEs.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairman, I declare that I serve as advisor to both the Visual, Audio, Creative Content Professional Association, and the National Instructors and Coaches Association.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In that capacity, I wish to convey feedback on Government procurement practices.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the creative and media sectors, payment upon project completion remains common.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While administratively straightforward, this places significant cash flow strains on smaller firms and freelancers.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Subcontractors and freelance professionals often bear financial risk despite delivering interim milestones.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These will help ease cash flow pressures and support industry sustainability.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairman, fiscal prudence is also about timing and structure.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Strengthening reserve stewardship, improve disbursement timing and promoting fair procurement can enhance both stability and fairness on the ground.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Members for their cuts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, sound public finance is not just about balanced budgets, fiscal rules and safeguards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For us, it is something more, and that is captured in MOF's motto which is: to create a better Singapore through finance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The flip side of this is that public finance has to be handled with great care and responsibility, because how it is used determines how the country moves forward and how the lives of Singaporeans can be improved.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, let me touch on the principles that underpin our approach to public finance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We must spend wisely and within our means.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is not only to meet current needs, but also to maximise our fiscal space to seize new opportunities for growth and have the ability to deal with future challenges or crises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Every public dollar represents the hard work of our people, that has been entrusted to the Government to use for the national good.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to achieve more and deliver better outcomes for Singaporeans and Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Public funding should do more than fill gaps.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It should drive new directions, accelerate growth and unlock momentum.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our goal is for finance to enable impact and catalyse innovation and transformation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are in a position of fiscal strength today, because of decades of careful stewardship and forward fiscal planning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I agree with Mr Lee Hong Chuang that our fiscal decisions today should preserve sufficient buffers and policy flexibility for future generations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We regularly review our tax system to strengthen our revenue base to meet rising needs, while ensuring that the system remains progressive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Taken together, our fiscal system strikes a balance between supporting short-term needs, and growing our reserves in line with the economy to provide a steady stream of income over the long term, as well as acting as a buffer against future shocks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As the Prime Minister has mentioned in the Budget debate, our revenue upsides have been used to address both our current and future needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In addition to permanent schemes, we have provided significant one-off support to Singaporeans in the past few years to deal with cost-of-living pressures and also funded investments across many areas, ranging from social needs to our economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ultimately, our revenue and expenditure considerations are anchored on fiscal responsibility.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MOF remains committed in ensuring that our current and future needs can be met in a fiscally sound and sustainable manner.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Statutory Boards may hold some reserves to support their capital investment and working capital needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where Statutory Boards have reserves, they invest their reserves in accordance with their liquidity needs and risk appetites.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Accountant-General's Department (AGD) has developed schemes to allow Statutory Boards to enjoy economies of scale and easier access to appointed fund managers and investment consultants through AGD's Demand Aggregation Programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to review ways to enhance our central support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked how MOF strengthens programme evaluation and scrutiny over high-value projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These processes continue to be key in delivering better, value-for-money outcomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, we work with agencies on programme evaluation and review.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Agencies are required to map how interventions and underlying assumptions translate to the desired outcomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Agencies are also required to develop evaluation plans with indicators that track implementation, outcomes and costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Besides enabling systematic tracking through these metrics, the evaluation plans specify clear milestone-based reporting.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These help us to understand whether a programme is achieving its objectives, whether improvements are needed and facilitates resourcing decisions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also asked if there have been reviews that allow us to re-allocate resources dynamically.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As our operating environment changes, MOF works with agencies to redesign programmes and pivot resources to new priorities when appropriate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package is one example.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Technological advancements are increasingly transforming business models and jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We saw a need to encourage companies to undertake enterprise and workforce transformation in tandem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, the support for workforce transformation programmes could be better coordinated and the utilisation of initiatives, such as the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit improved.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under the Workforce Development Grant, we will also provide more support for job redesign.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also worked with MOM to redesign the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit to make it easier for companies to use the credits and strengthen incentives for companies to upskill their employees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For high-value projects, MOF applies an additional layer of scrutiny across the whole of Government, to evaluate their worthiness and cost-effectiveness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Specialised committees support the review of big-ticket information and communications technology and smart system, and cybersecurity projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under the Gateway Process, larger-scale and more complex infrastructure projects are reviewed by MOF and the Development Projects Advisory Panel (DPAP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These committees include independent third parties, such as industry practitioners and experts, with deep technical expertise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Gateway Process remains an integral part of how we ensure value-for-money.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As part of our efforts to continuously improve, MOF has recently streamlined the Gateway Process to speed up project approvals while retaining the rigour that has helped us achieve value for money.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also aptly spoke about the role of finance as a catalyst.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, MOF uses public finance to catalyse growth and innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In every Budget, we deploy our fiscal resources strategically to drive effective change – we have invested heavily to build Singaporeans' long-term capabilities, through lifelong learning and the adoption of AI, as well as strengthened our enterprise ecosystem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MOF will continue to develop new solutions, working in partnership with the community and businesses, to address current and future challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: An example is how Tote Board supports community-driven innovations in social services, health and community care.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Last year, we announced the third tranche of the Tote Board's Enabling Lives Initiative Grant to support innovation for the disability sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Working with SG Enable, the first grant call has seen a diverse slate of proposals receiving support, ranging from community and independent living initiatives, to training and employment programmes for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong raised a cut on property tax valuation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As I understand it, he is suggesting that the valuation of an owner-occupied residential property for property tax purposes should be derived differently from non-owner-occupied property.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: His proposal is that while valuation of properties that are rented out should be using AV, which is based on rental transactions, owner-occupied properties should instead be based on "capital value" derived from sale transactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One should adopt the same valuation basis for all residential properties, regardless of whether it is owner-occupied, rented out or vacant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is so that there is a common yardstick to assess properties for property tax purposes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, having regard to the need for a common yardstick, the real question is whether one should use rental data for all residential properties or sales data for all residential properties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is because there are more rental transactions than sale transactions, which provides a more accurate and stable picture of comparable properties to determine the valuation of a given property.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Rents are also generally less volatile and subject to less variability compared to sale prices, as the rents are locked in by the lease agreements over a period of time, and hence, they are less impacted by market sentiments and the property cycle.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, just because a neighbour may have a better or a more nicely developed home that commands a higher rental or AV does not mean that the neighbour who has a simpler home will have the same AV because, obviously, when valuing, adjustments will have to be made to take into account the necessary attributes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, it is also important to distinguish between the valuation and the property tax rate in the determination of property tax payable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a concession to owner-occupied properties, property tax rates for owner-occupied properties are lower compared to non-owner-occupied properties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: From time to time, we also provide one-off property tax rebates for owner-occupied properties to help cushion the impact of the property tax.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This means that the retiree is also not taxed as if he is a landlord while the neighbourhood gentrifies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The fact of the matter is that when a neighbourhood is revitalised, the attractiveness of the retiree's property would increase, and one can expect both rent and sale prices to increase, that is, both the AV and the capital value will go up.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong also cited the use of sales data for sale of state land.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Sales data is appropriate for use where there is a sale of land or property, as sales data would be more directly relevant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes the sale of state land to HDB for public housing development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For AV, rental data is more appropriate for the reasons explained earlier.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, we are stewards of our reserves, assets and resources.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Singaporeans, it is our collective responsibility to make the best use of our resources for ourselves and for future generations, just as the previous generations did for us.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Let us create a better Singapore through finance together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Chairman, let me start by addressing Ms Tin Pei Ling's question on the Government's efforts to support businesses by streamlining regulatory requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The Economic Strategy Review (ESR) committees have engaged many business leaders to gather feedback on Singapore's long-term economic strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Many business leaders, here and abroad, have emphasised the importance of Singapore's reputation as a well-governed, stable place for doing business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our clear and consistent rules and laws are a competitive edge for us, especially in today's uncertain global economic environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Besides the ESR, I am also part of the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Pro-Enterprise Rules Review chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister, which oversees efforts to improve regulatory efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: MOF agencies are strongly supporting the Inter-Ministerial Committee’s efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This will reduce their cost burden and improve cash flow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: While we do want to keep compliance requirements proportionate, some regulations which balance between business and consumer interests require a little bit more careful consideration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, for example, Mr Kenneth Tiong asked if IRAS can review the concession for F&B establishments and hotels to display prices that exclude GST.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The purpose of this concession is to simplify processes for establishments that impose service charges, which includes both F&B establishments as well as hotels and this is because service charges are variable and may be waived or reduced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This concession has been in place for the last 30 years and it has become the accepted norm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Making an industry-wide change will require such businesses to incur additional costs when the industry is currently facing cost pressures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Nonetheless, we will review this in the future, to take into account technological improvements as well as business and consumer preferences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Edward Chia and Mr Shawn Loh suggested that the Government review the frequency of the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme payouts, citing how annual payouts may result in cashflow constraints for smaller businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: MOM annualises Progressive Wage Credit Scheme payouts because the wages of workers in the Progressive Wage Model sectors can vary throughout the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Smoothening the payout on an annual basis ensures that we provide sufficient, fair and consistent support to companies that are implementing wage increases to uplift our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, it is not a technical issue, it is a policy issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We, nevertheless, recognise that smaller businesses face cost pressures and cashflow constraints, which is why we have provided the Corporate Income Tax Rebate and Cash Grant to support more companies in this year's Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about the ASEAN Single Window and I managed to hear all of her cuts before her mic was cut off.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The ASEAN Single Window enables the exchange of documents for cross-border trade across ASEAN member states.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The onboarding of ASEAN Member States to the ASEAN Single Window has reduced paperwork, shortened clearance times and improved predictability and transparency for traders and exporters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This has facilitated trade by reducing cross-border friction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Singapore chairs the Steering Committee for the implementation of the ASEAN Single Window.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We are now exploring ASEAN Single Window 2.0, to strengthen interoperability and to expand electronic trade-related document exchanges to partners, such as China, Japan and South Korea and this could include adopting standardised technologies that allow for more types of electronic documents to be exchanged.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: These improvements to cross-border clearance processes will make it even easier for businesses to use Singapore as a launchpad to grow and expand internationally – in line with the recommendations from the ESR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about how the Government can help businesses catalyse innovation and enhance processes to be more productive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We encourage businesses to use more technology to increase productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For instance, SMEs that do not have large back-office teams can digitalise their processes to reduce paperwork and errors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: To support this effort, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) launched InvoiceNow, Singapore’s e-invoicing network, in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: By using InvoiceNow, this business can automatically issue e-invoices and populate accounting records, without having to spend time on manual data entry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Many businesses and trade associations have given us positive feedback that they were able to reduce invoicing errors using InvoiceNow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For businesses with overseas operations, cross-border B2B transactions will also be easier through InvoiceNow as its underlying e-invoicing standard is internationally accepted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For these reasons, the Government has been nudging more businesses to use InvoiceNow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We provide newly incorporated businesses with one year of free InvoiceNow services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Since 1 November 2025, newly incorporated companies that voluntarily register for the GST are required to transmit invoice data to IRAS via the InvoiceNow network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Such companies have benefited from faster GST audits and refunds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We will prioritise the onboarding of smaller businesses so that we can support them better in their transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: First, we will make a suite of InvoiceNow-Ready software: solutions available to businesses free-of-charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: More details on the timeline and support provided will be released by IRAS and IMDA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Turning to personal taxes, Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about reviewing the $20,000 threshold for personal income tax exemptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: While the personal income tax exemption threshold has not been changed for some time, this threshold should be seen together with our overall system of tax rates, tax reliefs and rebates that applies to all individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And among those who do, about eight in 10 have an effective tax rate of less than 6%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, I would like to reassure Mr Saktiandi that we will regularly review our income tax system to ensure that it is progressive and resilient, and that the tax burden is kept low, particularly and especially for middle- and lower-income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Ng Shi Xuan suggested providing tax credits to recognise our NSmen and caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As Mr Ng pointed out, we do have various tax reliefs in place to recognise NSmen and caregiving, or caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: To complement the tax reliefs, both NSmen and caregivers are also eligible for cash grants and credits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Cash grants and credits are administratively simpler and more progressive than tax credits which are tied to payable taxes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For example, we provide up to $18,500 in LifeSG credits and top-ups to CPF and Post-Secondary Education accounts via the NS Home Awards for operationally-ready NSmen, and we also have provided one-off NS LifeSG credits in 2022 and 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Caregivers can also apply for the Home Caregiving Grant to defray the cost of caregiving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We will continue to review the support provided to NSmen and caregivers, whether through tax deductions, cash grants, or other means to recognise them for their contributions and sacrifices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Temasek's mandate is to deliver good, sustainable long-term returns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Their returns contribute to the annual Budget via the Net Investment Returns framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As a principle, we want Temasek to operate on a commercial basis and optimise their returns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As Mr Lye acknowledges, the Government does not prescribe specific areas of investment or dictate Temasek's individual investment decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Nonetheless, Temasek is indeed a valuable partner for the Government in our economic growth strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And we work together whenever there is alignment on the three pathways that Mr Lye highlighted: identifying strategic areas for investment, growing our local champions and developing Singaporean talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Chairman, in an increasingly competitive global landscape, being pro-enterprise is essential to Singapore's continued economic relevance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: MOF is systematically improving our regulatory environment to reduce compliance costs and respond to business needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We will continue to closely partner businesses, industry associations and unions to maintain Singapore's position as one of the best places in the world to do business.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Chairman, I will speak on how MOF is making Government procurement more accessible for businesses and how technology can enhance public service delivery and accountability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: When procuring goods and services, the Government selects solutions that provide value for money so that we can achieve more and deliver better outcomes with public funds.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: When considering value for money, we take a holistic assessment of both benefits and costs, which can encompass economic, social and environmental outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: I appreciate Ms Denise Phua's and Ms Yeo Wan Ling's suggestions to embed social value and look into outcomes beyond cost in our procurement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Our holistic approach towards value for money allows us to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: To illustrate, in a tender for contact centre services by the Public Service Division, the awarded contractor was required to hire persons with disabilities and seniors for at least 10% of the jobs created by the contract.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We will continue to look for opportunities to reap positive economic, social and environmental outcomes, while achieving value for money and avoiding excessive compliance costs for businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Shawn Loh and Ms Denise Phua spoke about making Government procurement more accessible for SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked for an update on extension of Tender Lite to ICT procurement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: To improve accessibility, Government agencies ensure our procurement opportunities are appropriately sized to allow SMEs to participate while ensuring it is sufficient for suppliers to invest in innovative solutions or technology that improve productivity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Last year, we announced two initiatives to make procurement opportunities more accessible: expanding Tender Lite to construction and ICT procurement; and introducing the new Innovative Procurement Partnership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We implemented Tender Lite first for the procurement of general goods and services and then expanded to construction procurement in May 2025.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MOF has been working closely with industry stakeholders to expand Tender Lite to ICT procurement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We have incorporated feedback from SBF, the Association for Small and Medium Enterprises (ASME) and SGTech.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MOF will also remove the need for security deposits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: These changes will ease businesses' cashflow and reduce the risks that they bear.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: With the expansion of Tender Lite to ICT contracts, Tender Lite will cover all procurement with tender value up to $1 million.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MOF recognises the need to foster innovation and has been supporting the procurement of innovative solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Last year, we have taken this further and introduced the Innovative Procurement Partnership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This initiative enables public agencies to collaborate with businesses to test innovative solutions and provides assurance to businesses of the opportunity to scale up if the pilot testing is successful.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: To make the Innovative Procurement Partnership more accessible to SMEs and startups, established track records are not a requirement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The Government will also share risks with businesses by removing the need for security deposits and liquidated damages by default during the pilot testing phase.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: In addition, the Innovative Procurement Partnership is conducted via open sourcing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MOF provides Government agencies with contract templates and guidelines on payment milestones, including increasing the number of payment milestones where appropriate to ease cashflow.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: These templates and guidelines are developed with inputs from businesses and Government agencies to reflect industry norms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: For example, when procuring design services, Government agencies are required to specify the expected iterations of changes to allow the supplier to better price their bids.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Ms Denise Phua and Mr Shawn Loh asked how MOF agencies are harnessing technology, such as AI, to strengthen governance and improve the experience for businesses and citizens when transacting with Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling also suggested refreshing GeBIZ, our centralised e-procurement portal for Government agencies and Mr Ng Shi Xuan suggested incorporating AI into our procurement processes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We are committed to continuously making improvements and one such opportunity is with GeBIZ.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: GeBIZ was introduced in 2000 to digitalise procurement processes and consolidate Government quotations and tenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Businesses can access Government procurement opportunities and submit their proposals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Over the years, we have continuously enhanced GeBIZ.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: For instance, we implemented GeBIZ Supplier File Repository in 2024 to enable suppliers to use a single set of documents across multiple bids, reducing duplicative work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Moving forward, we will tap on the latest technology to comprehensively refresh GeBIZ system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The refreshed GeBIZ will go beyond the sourcing stage, covering pre-sourcing and contract management stages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This will consolidate systems that are currently operating separately and make procurement even more transparent, effective and efficient.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We invite businesses, who are interested, to sign up for the engagement when we send out the invitations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: A development that we will harness is the increasing capability of AI systems, which are becoming more widely used across businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: AI can significantly improve productivity if well implemented.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Beyond procurement, we are also leveraging AI in other areas of finance and governance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: For finance and audit, we trialled the use of AI, on top of data analytics, to obtain insights from large volumes of data.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We will continue to harness technology and leverage appropriate AI tools to enhance public service delivery and accountability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: (In Mandarin): MOF will ensure that the Government procurement processes remain fair and transparent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We will continue to introduce measures to assist enterprises participate more easily in Government tender activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: In addition, we will make good use of technology to make business transactions with the Government more efficient and simpler.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We will continue to work with trade associations, chambers of commerce and industry players to collect feedback and continuously optimise the transaction process between enterprises and the Government, helping the businesses save money, effort and time. : Mr Chairman, MOF remains committed to create a better Singapore through finance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We will continue to ensure fiscal prudence and sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Advance a pro-enterprise environment where regulatory requirements are streamlined to reduce compliance costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: These efforts will enable us to serve Singaporeans and businesses better.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: One clarification for Senior Minister of State Siow.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: So, what determines nominality, if that is the standard for qualifying for concession?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: And that IRAS has to police this at all suggests that the concession creates more complexity than it resolves, which brings us back to the question of whether it truly serves consumer interest.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: I think he is referring to a specific case in 2022 against a specific F&B establishment.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: However, it does not mean that the existing concession is no longer relevant to businesses.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: I had a point in my second cut, which was not delivered, on whether MOF would consider extending AI subscription tools for businesses in the same spirit as for individuals.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: Because AI business tools are naturally different from that for individuals.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Who would like to respond to Mr Ng?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: That is something that we will definitely look into.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: If found useful, we will definitely then open it for use and allow other businesses to use it as well.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: This will definitely save on the development cost and also the use cost as well, and we will most certainly take that suggestion as well.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If there are no further clarifications, I would like to invite Mr Sakiandi Supaat to withdraw your amendment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: First of all, I am convinced that there is discipline just now in the replies on how we spent, rigour in how we evaluate and adaptable in how we design our systems, so I will take this opportunity to thank Minister Indranee, Senior Minister of State, Acting Minister Jeffery Siow and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Shawn Huang for answering all our questions, 14 cuts and 10 speakers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And on that note, I also would like to thank the Permanent Secretary, MOF, and all the MOF staff behind the scenes who have been helping out to make this possible as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: On that note Chairman, I seek to leave to withdraw my amendment.
